why: W1-04 reported 9 NPC topic ids with no body anywhere. Six of them are real and all six are
on `game/data/npcs/writ-house.json` — the opening cell, the two people the player meets
before they have a name, a sheet or a quest. Those six keywords were offered by the only
two mouths in the game at that moment and answered by nothing.
THE OTHER THREE WERE AN ARTEFACT OF THE AUDIT, not of the data. `the chapter's vote`,
`the interior's consent` and `the ledger's terms` on mainline.json resolve perfectly well:
`game/src/core/topics.js#topicKey` folds an apostrophe into the word (`the chapters vote`)
and the bodies exist in 50-mainline.json as `the-chapters-vote`, `the-interiors-consent`
and `the-ledgers-terms`. The audit used its own slug, which split on the apostrophe. An
audit that does not use the runtime's own key function reports gaps the runtime does not
have — worth more than the three topics it cost.
Rules followed, from 50-mainline.json and 55-utility.json: at least two infos from
different actor archetypes; the LAST info on every topic ungated, so a keyword once known
is never a silence; `to` is the AddTopic graph `sim/quest/topic-supply.js` reads, and every
target here already has a body. Nothing states a solution — these are the first six things
anyone says to you, and the first thing this game has to establish is what you are.

topics.note: jeeh-ei, in the barge hold, before the player has a name. The one topic answered by somebody with nothing to gain from answering.

infos.x: Egg-sibling. Sit against the ribs, not the boards — the boards sweat and you will be wet the whole crossing. We came up from the yards at Lilmoth. Nobody has told us where we are going and nobody is going to, so I have stopped asking and started counting the tides.

Twenty-six of us and four benches. Do not stand when she rolls. The scribe up top has a list with all of us on it and when he reads it out you say the name he reads, not the one you were given — that is the only advice worth what it costs.
The hold of a writ barge. It is not a prison, they will tell you, because a prison would want a charge written down. It is a room that goes where the Office sends it.
The hold is where they keep people who are being moved rather than held. There is a difference on the paper and there is no difference in the room.

topics.note: jeeh-ei. RI-CHR02's naming question, asked by a person instead of by a menu.

infos.x: Mine is Jeeh-Ei and my mother chose it out of the water she chose it in, and the Office writes it Jeeh E. with a stop, as though the second half were a clerk's mistake. Keep yours. Say the other one to them and keep yours.

You would not have one. It is the name the water gives, and it is three sounds long, and it does not fit in the box on their form — so they take it off you at the desk and hand you back something they can file. That is the first thing they take. It is not the last.
The Office calls it a preferred appellation. There is a column for it on the intake sheet and the column is four characters wide, which tells you what the Office thinks a name is for.
A hatch-name. What the Saxhleel are called by their own before anyone writes anything down. Ask one of them and you will be told; ask a scribe and you will be told what it costs to change it.

topics.note: warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma. The document the whole opening turns on, described by the man who fills it in.

infos.x: This one? This one is yours. A writ of works: it says the Provincial Office has an interest in your labour and that the interest is satisfied at a date the writ does not name. It is four lines and one of them is a date and the date is blank. That is the whole of the instrument.

You want to know whether it is lawful. It is lawful. Everything difficult about it is lawful, and the part that is not lawful is that the amendment book has been open at the same page for two years and nobody has signed the other side of it.
Paper the Office issues instead of a sentence. The Assize does not enforce them and the Assize does not stop them either, which is a position, whatever the Assize calls it.
A writ. If you are carrying one you are working it off; if you are carrying two you are somebody's problem. Do not lose it — the copy the Office keeps is not the one that gets read.

topics.note: warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma. A Saxhleel clerk filling in writs for Saxhleel, which is the whole character in one topic.

infos.x: You are looking at my hands and not at my face, and that is fair. I write the intake and I write the transfers and I write the ones that come back. Sixty-one this season. I know what you are going to ask and the answer is that somebody writes them either way, and the one who writes them can spell a name right.
Intake, transfer, return. Three books and one desk. I have held this desk eight years and in that time the Office has changed the form twice and the arrangement not at all.

Tuleeh-Ma keeps the Tidewrack intake. Cleanest hand in the province and the only one who files the returns on the day they happen, which is why the Office has never once looked at his books and why he wants them looked at.
He writes down who comes off the barges. Somebody has to, and if you would rather it were nobody, go and stand at Tidewrack for a morning and see what nobody looks like.

topics.note: warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma. The intake roll — and the thing `the-shadowscale-list` is quietly not.

infos.x: The intake roll. Every body off every barge, in the order they came up the stair, with the name they gave and the name the Office assigned beside it. Two columns, and it is the second one that follows you. I read it out at the top of the hour and you answer to whichever one I say.
There is more than one list and I will only name this one. Ask a warden about the other, and ask them somewhere I am not standing.
Whose list? Everyone here is on a list. The trick is being on the boring one — the boring one gets read out and the interesting one gets acted on.
The intake list at Tidewrack. If your name is on it you came off a barge, and if you came off a barge there is a writ somewhere with your labour on it.

topics.note: warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma. The word for an Argonian raised among the Empire, said by one to a stranger. Ungated last row keeps it answerable to anyone who has heard it.

infos.x: Say it to me if you like. I have been called it by people who meant it as an insult and by people who meant it as a fact, and the second sort are harder. I was hatched in Gideon, I write Cyrodilic, and the marsh does not stop being mine because of either.
It is our word, not yours, and it means assimilated — one of us raised among you. You will hear it used gently by the Office and hard by the deep villages, and both of them are talking about me.
Lukiul. Tame. It is not a curse and I will not pretend it is a kindness. It means the ones who came back speaking the other language and could not say why the wells matter.
An Argonian word. It means one of them brought up in an imperial town — a clerk, a scribe, a legionary. Half the province is one and the other half has an opinion about it.
